statusText:
The CME weekend halt still frames everything. NQ has not quoted since the weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August and will not quote again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about four hours beyond the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail is 11% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

What moved this hour is the shape of the conflict, not the price. The dominant weekend thread has rotated from the Strait of Hormuz to Lebanon. Two Israeli airstrikes killed at least eleven people in southern Lebanon, Hezbollah publicly condemned Netanyahu for seeking to escalate the war, and Netanyahu's office then accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire by attacking soldiers inside the security zone and seriously wounding three of them. A second active front opening while the strait remains blockaded is a real escalation vector, and it is the reason Stress rises again rather than decaying.

Against that sit genuine de-escalation headlines. House Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News the Iran conflict 'is going to be settling soon' and would stabilise oil and gas prices - though he made the same call in March and it did not hold. Iran and Oman have still not agreed on reopening Hormuz despite earlier optimism, the UAE condemned a further hostile attack on an ADNOC-associated vessel on Friday evening, Houthi forces hit the Red Sea port of Mokha with six ballistic missiles killing three, and a Russian tanker leak is now smearing about 7.5 miles of Oman's coastline. This is a genuinely two-sided tape waiting for a venue to price it, which is exactly the configuration that belongs in Stress at 62% (elevated) rather than in Tail.

The last hard marks remain Friday's: NQ futures 30,141.75 (-0.15%), the Nasdaq-100 cash index 30,046.14 (-0.13%), VIX 14.25 (-2.60%), 10-year 4.696% and 2-year 4.171%, WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). Equity vol is priced for calm while oil is priced for a supply war - the IEA now expects the widest 2026 shortfall in five years at 4.3 million barrels a day. That divergence is the single most important unresolved thing on the board, and it will be resolved at the reopen, not before.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 11% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to protect against while the venue is closed - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. Treat Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart as the single checkpoint that matters: it is the first opportunity for two days of two-sided Middle East headlines to be priced at once, and it is the anchor of the danger window rather than any point inside this horizon. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail at 11% and status green, but the conflict rotates to Lebanon and Stress climbs to 62% into Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The entire 24-hour horizon sits inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every input in the price column is a Friday close carried forward, which is the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 64% (solid) rather than higher.

Friday's marks: NQ futures settled 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, having opened at 30,210.75 and traded a 30,028.50-30,283.00 range on 397,964 contracts, closing near the middle of that range against a 52-week span of 22,961.50-30,975.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 30,046.14, off 0.13%, in a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range. Neither is a stressed tape; both are consolidation prints a fraction below the highs.

Cross-asset: VIX closed 14.25, down 2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 range and close to the bottom of its 13.38-35.30 52-week band. That is equity volatility priced for nothing to happen. The 10-year yield finished 4.696% and the 2-year 4.171%, a positive but unremarkable spread with no curve signal demanding attention. Crude is the outlier: WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%), up roughly 5% on the week, 3.5% on the month and 33% on the year, with the IEA warning of a 4.3 million barrel-a-day supply decline in 2026 - the widest shortfall in five years. A 14-handle VIX alongside a 33% annual move in crude is the definition of a conflicting cross-asset signal, and the prompt is explicit that conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail.

Geopolitics, the only thing genuinely new this hour: the Lebanon front has reactivated. Israeli airstrikes killed at least eleven people in southern Lebanon; Israel accused Hezbollah of 'using its own civilians as human shields'; Hezbollah replied that the strikes reflect the 'desire and will of the criminal enemy Prime Minister Netanyahu to escalate the war' for domestic political reasons; and Netanyahu's office then said Hezbollah attacked soldiers in the security zone and 'seriously injured three of our soldiers'. Separately the UAE condemned a hostile Iranian attack on an ADNOC-associated vessel on Friday evening - the third such ship in two days - Houthi forces fired six ballistic missiles at the Yemeni Red Sea port of Mokha killing at least three and suspending operations, and Bandar Abbas airport resumed domestic flights. The counterweight is Speaker Johnson's 'settling soon' claim and the continuing, unconcluded Iran-Oman corridor talks.

Why Tail stays at 11%: the definition requires observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements or NQ holding near extremes. None of those can be observed because nothing is quoting, and the prompt forbids treating hypothetical post-event alignment as already observed. Gap risk at a reopen four hours outside this horizon is not a within-horizon one-way path.

Why Stress rises to 62%: a second military front has opened while the first is unresolved, shipping attacks continued into Friday evening, the oil market is already carrying a war premium that equity vol has not acknowledged, and two full days of headlines will be repriced in a single illiquid Sunday-evening auction. Stress is the right home for all of it, and it should not decay while that remains ahead.

Why Confidence is 64%: the calendar, the geopolitical thread and every cross-asset level were read from primary sources this hour and cross-checked, but the newest price evidence is over 30 hours old and no live path exists to corroborate any of it. Solid, not high.

Dominant mode is mixed: escalation and de-escalation headlines are running simultaneously, oil and equity vol disagree, and there is no tape to arbitrate between them.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours contain no tradeable price action after Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close. Claude published 23 of 24 hourly assessments, with only the 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August missing. Tail never left the low band, ranging 2-11% and holding EA_ON green throughout. The informative movement is in Stress: it collapsed to 9-14% in the dead hours immediately after the Friday close, then climbed steadily from 45% at 00:34 UTC to 60% by 18:25 UTC as weekend geopolitical headlines accumulated with no venue to price them. Confidence improved in parallel, from 36% overnight to 63%, as successive runs verified Friday's closes, the cross-asset picture and the seven-day calendar from primary sources.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are entirely inside the CME halt, so the forecast is a headline-accumulation path rather than a price path. Tail stays in the low band throughout, 10-13%, keeping EA_ON and green in every slot; it drifts fractionally higher only in the final hours as Sunday's restart approaches. Stress eases to 60% through the quiet overnight window, then rebuilds to 66% across Sunday as the reopen nears and two days of Lebanon, Hormuz and shipping headlines queue up for a single illiquid auction. Confidence dips to 60% overnight on pure staleness - the newest hard marks will be more than 30 hours old - and recovers to 66% on Sunday as Gulf and Asian shipping data provide the first genuinely new information since Friday. The real checkpoint, the 22:00 UTC Sunday restart, sits four hours beyond this horizon and is where the danger window is anchored.

forecastDetail.comment: CME is dark and stays dark: NQ has not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and will not quote again until roughly 22:00 UTC Sunday, four hours past the end of this horizon. No venue is printing, so no pathological one-way path can form and Tail holds at 11%. Stress at 62% carries the weekend headline load, not price.

Saturday evening European hours. The live thread is Lebanon, not Hormuz: Israeli strikes killed at least eleven in the south, Hezbollah wounded three Israeli soldiers in the security zone and Netanyahu's office is calling it a ceasefire violation. A second front reopening while the strait is still blockaded is a genuine escalation vector, but it accrues to Stress with the tape shut.

Late European evening, thinning wire flow. Expect the Lebanon exchange and the ADNOC vessel attack claims to keep circulating without independent confirmation. Tail unchanged at 11%; Stress steady at 62% because nothing here is yet a transmission channel into equities.

US evening. Headline risk stays two-sided: Speaker Johnson's claim that the war 'is going to be settling soon' sits directly against the IRGC's conditions and Gharibabadi's line that the blockade holds until Washington accepts defeat. Conflicting signals of this kind belong in Stress, which eases marginally to 61% as the news cycle quiets.

Overnight into Sunday. Weekend desks are empty and the Gulf morning has not started. Confidence slips toward 62% purely on evidence staleness — the newest hard price marks are now more than thirty hours old and nothing will refresh them before the reopen.

Sunday pre-dawn UTC. Gulf and Asian mornings begin producing shipping and tanker-tracking data, the first genuinely new information since Friday. Tail stays 11% with no quotes; Stress eases to 60% on the absence of overnight escalation, which is the base case rather than a forecast of calm.
